summary: Coins and what they buy, how to price and swap goods, and the rules for objects, poisons and magic items: attunement, wearing, activating and sentient items.
The six abilities and how a roll turns them into results: ability checks, advantage and disadvantage, the proficiency bonus and saving throws.
Rules for exploration and downtime: keeping time, travelling, environmental hazards, traps, diseases and madness, resting, and what characters do between adventures.
How a fight is run: turn order, moving and acting, making attacks, cover, damage and healing, and special cases such as mounts and underwater fights.
How magic works at the table: what a spell is, how slots and preparation limit casting, and the steps and options for casting a spell.
Background for campaigns that range across worlds: sample pantheons of gods from history and myth, and the planes of existence.
A table of how the coin types convert into one another.
How to treat an object as a target: its armor class, its hit points and the damage it takes.
The ways a poison is delivered, with sample poisons and their prices and effects.
How a character bonds with a magic item that calls for it, the limit on attuned items, and how attunement ends.
What counts as wearing or wielding a magic item, how many items of a kind work at once, and how paired items work.
The ways a magic item is triggered: command words, consumables, spells and charges.
Items with a mind of their own: how to generate their abilities, senses, alignment and purpose, and what happens when their will conflicts with the wielder's.
How an ability score is turned into the modifier that is added to rolls.
Rolling a second d20 and keeping the higher or lower result, what grants each, and how several sources combine.
The level-based bonus that applies to skills, saving throws and attacks a character is trained in, and the limits on how it is added.
How a check is rolled, typical difficulty classes, contests, the skills tied to each ability, passive checks, and working together or as a group.
What each of the six abilities covers in play, with the checks, attack and damage rolls, carrying capacity, armor, hit points and spellcasting that each one drives.
The roll made to resist a harmful effect, how the ability and the difficulty class are chosen, and the effect of proficiency.
The scales of time used in play: rounds in a fight, minutes while exploring, and hours or days while travelling.
Speed over longer distances: travel pace and its effects, difficult terrain, forced marches, climbing, swimming, crawling and jumping.
Hazards of the surroundings: falling, suffocating, vision and light, the senses that see in the dark, food and water, and interacting with objects.
Running traps: how they are triggered, found and disabled, their effects and save DCs, damage by severity, complex traps, and a set of sample traps.
How a disease spreads and is endured, with the sample diseases cackle fever, sewer plague and sight rot.
Mind-shattering effects of three lengths, short-term, long-term and indefinite, with tables of effects and the ways to cure them.
What a short rest and a long rest are, how long each takes, and what a character regains from them.
Downtime between adventures: lifestyle costs, and activities such as crafting, working a trade, recuperating, researching and training.
The sequence of a fight: who is surprised, how initiative sets the turn order, and what a creature may do on its turn, including bonus actions, other activity and reactions.
Moving in a fight: splitting movement, difficult terrain, falling prone, passing other creatures, flying, creature size and space, squeezing through tight gaps, and handling nearby objects.
The actions open to a creature on its turn, such as attacking, casting a spell, dashing, disengaging, dodging, helping, hiding, readying, searching and using an object.
How an attack is resolved: the attack roll and its modifiers, unseen targets, ranged and melee attacks, opportunity attacks, fighting with two weapons, grappling and shoving.
How obstacles shield a target, and the defensive bonuses that half cover and three-quarters cover give, with total cover blocking targeting outright.

Hit points, damage rolls and critical hits, damage types, resistance and vulnerability, healing, and what happens at 0 hit points, including death saves, stabilizing, knockouts and temporary hit points.
Getting on and off a mount, and how a controlled or an independent mount behaves during a fight.
How fighting while immersed in water changes attacks and which damage is resisted.
Spell levels, spell slots, known and prepared spells, casting at a higher level, casting in armor, cantrips and rituals.
The elements of casting a spell: casting time, range, components, duration and concentration, targets, areas of effect, saving throws, attack rolls, combined effects and the schools of magic.
Sample pantheons from Celtic, Greek, Egyptian and Norse tradition, each with a list of deities.
The cosmology of the multiverse: the Material Plane, planar travel, and the transitive, inner and outer planes and demiplanes.
